title: What if you built your house underground
headline: WHAT IF YOUR HOUSE WAS UNDERGROUND?

shots.text: What if you built your house underground?
A few feet down, it's about 55 degrees all year, so heating costs way less.
But the roof has to hold up about a hundred tons of dirt.
And groundwater is always pushing to get in.
In Coober Pedy, Australia, about half the town lives underground!

youtube.title: What If You Built Your House Underground? 🏠 #shorts
youtube.description:
What if you built your whole house underground? 🤯

A few feet down, the ground stays about the same temperature all year (around 50 to 60°F in much of the US), so an underground house needs a lot less heating and cooling. But there's a catch: the roof has to hold up the dirt on top of it. Just one meter of wet soil over a small house weighs around a hundred tons, far more than any snow load. And groundwater is always pushing in from every side, so the whole house needs a thick waterproof shell and drains.

It's not just an idea: in Coober Pedy, South Australia, about half the town lives in underground homes called 'dugouts' to escape summer heat that can top 113°F. Inside, they stay at a comfortable 75°F or so all year 🌵

🏠 Would you live in one? Tell me in the comments.
